title: Presentations
about: Collocations for giving a talk: preparing it, using your body and voice, connecting with the audience and making good visual aids, such as target audience, make eye contact and bring a talk to life.

items.pattern: prepare a presentation / talk / speech · then give (or do) the presentation
items.meaning: plan and make a talk and its slides before you give it
items.example: Mum is **preparing a presentation** about the history of our street for her book club.
more: Our team leader asked me to **prepare a short presentation** on the new holiday rules.
It took Sam a week to **prepare his presentation** about saving energy at home.
items.watchOut: Prepare a presentation — створити її (план, текст, слайди); prepare for a presentation — готуватися до неї (репетирувати). «Приготувати» тут не cook: cook — лише про їжу. Виступити з презентацією — give a presentation, у розмові ще do / make a presentation.

items.pattern: your core message · get across / communicate your core message · also main / key message
items.meaning: the most important idea you want people to understand and remember
items.example: Before you make any slides, write your **core message** in one sentence.
more: Say your **core message** at the start and again at the end.
The charity's **core message** is simple: every child should be able to read.
items.watchOut: Message тут — не «повідомлення в телефоні», а головна думка, посил. «Головна думка» — core / main / key message, а не heart message.

items.pattern: the target audience (for / of sth) · aim a talk at an audience
items.meaning: the particular group of people you are speaking or writing for
items.example: The **target audience** for this talk is parents of children starting school.
more: The magazine's **target audience** is retired people who love gardening.
Jokes about exams won't work if your **target audience** is grandparents.
items.watchOut: Аудиторія (люди) — audience, а не auditory (прикметник «слуховий») і не auditorium (зал). Вимова: /ˈɔːdiəns/, «óдієнс», а не «аудієнс». Про всіх слухачів в одній залі — the audience, без -s.

items.pattern: hold / keep sb's attention · attract / catch / grab sb's attention · lose sb's attention
items.meaning: make people stay interested and keep listening
items.example: A good story at the start will help you **hold the audience's attention**.
more: Our history teacher could **keep the class's attention** with just a good story and a piece of chalk.
The film was so slow that it couldn't **hold my attention**.
items.watchOut: «Утримувати увагу» — hold / keep attention, а не support чи save attention. Привернути увагу (на початку) — attract / catch / grab attention; втратити — lose sb's attention.

items.pattern: an interactive presentation / talk / lesson / session / display
items.meaning: a presentation where the audience takes part, for example by answering questions or voting
items.uk: інтерактивна презентація, виступ із залученням слухачів
items.example: Her **interactive presentation** had everyone guessing prices and shouting out answers.
more: The museum guide gave an **interactive talk**, so the kids got to touch the old tools.
Our science museum has lots of **interactive displays** for kids.

items.pattern: connect with your audience / with people · make a connection with sb
items.meaning: build a feeling of understanding and sympathy between you and the people listening
items.example: She told us about her own first day at school, and that helped her **connect with the audience**.
more: The new head teacher really **connects with** the pupils: they all love her assemblies.
He's clever, but he struggles to **connect with** people he doesn't know.
items.watchOut: «Знайти контакт з аудиторією» — connect with your audience, а не find contact with the audience. Make contact with sb — просто зв'язатися з кимось (подзвонити, написати). Прийменник — with.

items.pattern: body language · positive / negative / open body language
items.meaning: the way you move, stand and hold your arms, which shows how you feel
items.example: Your **body language** says a lot before you even open your mouth.
more: You could tell from his **body language** that he didn't want to be at the wedding.
Good **body language** in a job interview means sitting up and smiling.
items.watchOut: Мова тіла — body language, а не language of the body чи body speech. Language тут незлічуване: без a і без -s.

items.pattern: stand / sit up straight · straight is an adverb here, no -ly
items.meaning: keep your back straight and your shoulders back
items.example: **Stand up straight** and look at the audience, not at the floor.
more: Grandma always told us to **sit up straight** at the table.
If you **sit up straight**, you'll sound more confident on the phone too.
items.watchOut: Straight тут — прислівник без -ly: stand up straight, не straightly. «Не сутулься!» — Don't slouch! або Sit up straight!

items.pattern: use / make hand gestures · a gesture
items.meaning: movements of your hands that help to show what you mean
items.example: A few **hand gestures** can help you show how big or small something is.
more: Italians are famous for using lots of **hand gestures** when they talk.
Small **hand gestures** look natural; big ones can look a bit theatrical.
items.watchOut: Gesture читається з «дж»: /ˈdʒestʃə/. «Жестикулювати» в розмові частіше use hand gestures або wave your hands about; gesticulate — книжне слово. Міміка — facial expressions, а не mimics.

items.pattern: make eye contact (with sb) · avoid eye contact
items.meaning: look directly into someone's eyes for a moment
items.uk: подивитися в очі, встановити зоровий контакт
items.example: When you **make eye contact** with people, they feel you're talking to them personally.
more: The waiter wouldn't **make eye contact** with us, so we waited ages for the bill.
Shy children often find it hard to **make eye contact** with adults.
items.watchOut: Eye contact — без артикля і з eye в однині: make eye contact, а не make an eye contact, eye contacts чи eyes contact. Дієслово — make, не do чи give.

items.pattern: maintain / keep / hold eye contact (with sb) · maintain is a bit more formal
items.meaning: keep looking into someone's eyes and not look away
items.uk: не відводити погляду, підтримувати зоровий контакт
items.example: It's polite to **maintain eye contact** when someone is talking to you.
more: He **kept eye contact** with the interviewer and answered every question calmly.
Try to **hold eye contact** with the person who asked the question while you answer.
items.watchOut: «Підтримувати контакт» — maintain / keep / hold, а не support: support — підтримувати когось (допомогою, грошима). У maintain наголос на другому складі: /meɪnˈteɪn/.

items.pattern: breathe deeply · take a deep breath
items.meaning: fill your lungs with air slowly and fully
items.example: When your hands start shaking, stop for a second and **breathe deeply**.
more: The doctor put the stethoscope on my back and told me to **breathe deeply**.
**Take a deep breath** and count to ten before you answer him.
items.watchOut: Breathe /briːð/ — дієслово «дихати», breath /breθ/ — іменник «подих». Тому breathe deeply, але take a deep breath.

items.pattern: speak clearly · speak slowly / loudly / clearly
items.meaning: speak so that every word is easy to hear and understand
items.example: In a big hall you need to **speak clearly** so the people at the back can hear.
more: Please **speak clearly** when you leave a message after the beep.
My grandad is a bit deaf, so I always **speak clearly** when I phone him.
items.watchOut: Після speak потрібен прислівник: speak clearly. Clear так вживають хіба що у сталому виразі loud and clear. Не плутай з cleanly — «чисто, охайно».

items.pattern: (sb's) tone of voice · in a calm / friendly / angry tone of voice
items.meaning: the sound of your voice, which shows how you feel: calm, angry, bored or excited
items.example: Your **tone of voice** tells people whether you're excited or bored.
more: I didn't like the **tone of voice** he used with the waiter.
On the phone, your **tone of voice** matters even more, because people can't see your face.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай кажуть in a … tone of voice: She said it in a friendly tone of voice. Тон — tone, а не tune: tune — мелодія.

items.pattern: public speaking · a fear of public speaking · be good at public speaking
items.meaning: the activity of speaking to a large group of people
items.uk: публічні виступи, вміння виступати перед людьми
items.example: Our daughter used to hate **public speaking**, but now she loves the school debating club.
more: My boss is brilliant at **public speaking**: she never uses notes.
Teachers do so much **public speaking** that they rarely get nervous.
items.watchOut: Публічні виступи як навичка — public speaking (незлічуване, без -s), а не public performances. Один конкретний виступ — a talk або a speech.

items.pattern: deal with questions / problems / complaints · deal – dealt – dealt
items.meaning: answer questions from people and handle them well
items.uk: відповідати на запитання, давати раду запитанням
items.example: Leave ten minutes at the end to **deal with questions**.
more: The head teacher **dealt with questions** from worried parents for over an hour.
She stays calm, so she's great at **dealing with tricky questions**.
items.watchOut: Deal у цьому значенні — завжди з with: deal with questions, не deal questions. Минулий час — dealt /delt/, не dealed.

items.pattern: listen carefully (to sb/sth) · also listen closely
items.meaning: listen with all your attention so that you understand
items.example: **Listen carefully** to the whole question before you start answering.
more: **Listen carefully**: the train to Brighton now leaves from platform six.
If you **listen carefully**, you can hear the sea from our balcony.
items.watchOut: Слухати когось / щось — listen to sb/sth: listen carefully to the question, не listen the question. Hear — просто чути звук, з carefully його зазвичай не вживають.

items.pattern: prepare / give out / hand out handouts · a handout
items.meaning: make printed pages with the main information for the audience to keep
items.example: I **prepared handouts** with the recipe so people could cook it at home.
more: The teacher **gave out handouts** with the new vocabulary at the end of the lesson.
Don't forget to **prepare handouts** for anyone who can't see the screen well.
items.watchOut: Роздатковий матеріал — handouts, а не distribution materials. Роздати — give out або hand out.

items.pattern: visual aids · use visual aids · a visual aid
items.meaning: pictures, charts, films or objects that help people understand a talk
items.example: The teacher used maps and old photos as **visual aids**.
more: A model of the bridge made a brilliant **visual aid** for his talk.
Without **visual aids**, a talk about the solar system is hard to follow.
items.watchOut: Наочні матеріали — visual aids, а не visual helps чи visible aids. Visible — «видимий», visual — «зоровий, наочний». Aid /eɪd/ — допомога, засіб.

items.pattern: make / have an impact on sb/sth · a big / real / huge impact
items.meaning: have a strong effect on people, so they notice and remember
items.example: Her letter to the local paper **made a real impact**: the council fixed the road within a month.
more: Moving to the countryside **had a huge impact on** our kids' health.
One kind teacher can **have a big impact on** a child's life.
items.watchOut: «Справити враження, вплинути» — make / have an impact on, а не give an impact чи do an impact. Прийменник — on: an impact on the audience. Наголос на першому складі: /ˈɪmpækt/.

items.pattern: PowerPoint slides · a slide · on a slide · a slide show
items.meaning: the pages of a presentation that are shown on a screen
items.example: Her talk on family history had about ten **PowerPoint slides**, mostly old photos.
more: Can you email me the **PowerPoint slides** after the meeting?
There's a spelling mistake on the third **slide**.
items.watchOut: Українською «презентація» часто означає сам файл: «скинь презентацію». Англійською можна send me the presentation, але часто кажуть the slides. Те, що написано на слайді, — зазвичай on the slide.

items.pattern: presentation software · use / learn presentation software
items.meaning: computer programs for making slides, such as PowerPoint
items.example: Our club secretary learnt to use **presentation software** at the age of seventy.
more: You don't need fancy **presentation software**: a few printed photos work too.
Most **presentation software** lets you add music and short videos.
items.watchOut: Software незлічуване: presentation software, без a і без -s (не softwares). «Софт» англійською — software, а не soft.

items.pattern: an effective presentation / talk / way of doing sth
items.meaning: a presentation that works well and gets the result you wanted
items.example: An **effective presentation** leaves people knowing exactly what to do next.
more: Short, real stories make a talk far more **effective** than lots of numbers.
Their presentation was so **effective** that the council agreed to build a new playground.
items.watchOut: Effective — той, що дає потрібний результат. Efficient — той, що працює швидко й без зайвих витрат (an efficient heater, an efficient worker). «Ефективна презентація» — effective, а не efficient.

items.pattern: keep sth simple / short / clear · keep it simple
items.meaning: not make something complicated or full of details
items.example: **Keep the design simple**: two colours and one font look far better than ten.
more: The doctor told me to **keep my meals simple** for a few days: rice, toast and bananas.
My advice for a first trip abroad: **keep it simple** and don't plan too much.
items.watchOut: Після keep + що — прикметник, а не прислівник: keep it simple, не keep it simply. Так само keep it short, keep calm.

items.pattern: easy / hard / difficult to read · a clear font
items.meaning: clear, so that your eyes can read it without effort
items.example: The new road signs are big, bright and **easy to read**, even at night.
more: The instructions were **easy to read**, so we put the wardrobe together in an hour.
My doctor's handwriting isn't exactly **easy to read**.
items.watchOut: «Легко читати» — easy to read, а не easy for reading чи light to read. Не easy to watch: watch — дивитися на те, що рухається (фільм, матч).

items.pattern: key points · also key issues / areas / elements / questions
items.meaning: the main and most important points
items.example: Write the **key points** on a card in case you forget them.
more: The leaflet sums up the **key points** of the new parking rules.
Price and location are the **key issues** for most people looking for a flat.
items.watchOut: «Ключові моменти» — key points, а не key moments: moment — це момент у часі. Big points так не кажуть; можна ще main points.

items.pattern: bullet points · in bullet points · a bullet point
items.meaning: short lines in a list, each with a dot or small mark in front of it
items.example: Each slide had a title and three short **bullet points**.
more: My CV has a few **bullet points** under each job.
The email listed what to bring in **bullet points**: boots, a raincoat and lunch.
items.watchOut: Маркований список — bullet points (bullet — «куля», за формою крапки). Українське «пункт» тут — point, а не paragraph.

items.pattern: follow sb's argument / explanation / reasoning
items.meaning: understand the reasons someone gives, one step after another
items.uk: стежити за чиєюсь думкою, розуміти хід думок
items.example: Slow down a bit. I'm finding it hard to **follow your argument**.
more: The article was so badly written that I couldn't **follow the argument** at all.
Draw a simple diagram: it'll help the class **follow your explanation**.
items.watchOut: Argument тут — хід думки, аргументація (в іншому контексті це ще й сварка). «Стежити за думкою» — follow, а не take чи watch.

items.pattern: a pie chart · on / in a pie chart · a slice of the pie chart
items.meaning: a circle divided into slices that show the parts of a whole
items.example: This **pie chart** shows how we spend our monthly budget.
more: The **pie chart** showed that most students walk to school.
Half the **pie chart** is blue, so half the class chose the beach.
items.watchOut: Кругова діаграма — a pie chart (pie — пиріг, порізаний на шматки), а не a circle diagram чи a cake chart. Diagram англійською — це радше схема чи креслення.

items.pattern: a bar chart · bar graph (especially American)
items.meaning: a chart with columns of different heights that show amounts
items.example: The **bar chart** compares how much rain fell each month.
more: Each bar in the **bar chart** shows one year of our electricity bills.
A **bar chart** makes it easy to see which flavour of ice cream sold best.
items.watchOut: Стовпчикова діаграма — a bar chart, а не a bar table чи a column diagram. Table — це таблиця з рядками й стовпцями.

items.pattern: bring sth to life · come to life
items.meaning: make something more interesting, lively and real
items.example: Old photos and a few funny stories **brought the talk to life**.
more: A good guide can **bring a boring old castle to life**.
The new lights have **brought the old market square to life** at night.
items.watchOut: «Оживити» — bring to life, а не carry to life чи bring into life. Після to — life без артикля.

warmup.explain: Аудиторія як слухачі — audience. Auditorium — це зал, auditory — прикметник «слуховий».

warmup.uk: Учителька вміє утримувати увагу дітей цілий урок.
warmup.q: The teacher knows how to ___ the children's attention for the whole lesson.
warmup.explain: Утримувати увагу — hold або keep attention. Support — підтримувати когось, а не увагу.

warmup.uk: На співбесіді дивися людині в очі.
warmup.q: In a job interview, ___ eye contact with the person you're talking to.
warmup.explain: Дивитися в очі — make eye contact, без артикля.

warmup.uk: Перед виступом зупинись і глибоко подихай.
warmup.q: Before you go on stage, stop and ___ deeply.

warmup.uk: Ці фото справили на нас сильне враження.
warmup.q: These photos ___ a big impact on us.
warmup.explain: Справити враження, вплинути — make або have an impact on. Give an impact так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Презентація була довга й повільна, але дуже ефективна: після неї всі купили квитки.
warmup.q: It was a long, slow presentation, but very ___: afterwards everyone bought tickets.
warmup.explain: Effective — дає результат. Efficient — працює швидко й економно. Affective — термін психології («емоційний»).
Після keep it — прикметник: keep it simple. Primitive — «примітивний», звучить зневажливо.

warmup.uk: Які ключові моменти цього договору оренди?
warmup.q: What are the key ___ in this rental agreement?
warmup.explain: Ключові моменти — key points. Moment — лише момент у часі.

A.q: Dan looks at the floor the whole time. He should ___ eye contact with a few people in the room.
A.explain: Make eye contact — подивитися людям в очі.

A.q: Jack wasn't afraid of the audience, but he panicked when it came to ___ with their questions.
A.explain: Deal with questions — відповідати на запитання, давати їм раду.
Stand up straight — стань рівно. Straight тут прислівник без -ly.

B.q: These instructions are for tourists, so keep the English ___.
B.explain: Keep sth simple — не ускладнювати. Після keep + що — прикметник.

B.q: Each slice of the ___ chart shows one way people get to work.
B.explain: Шматки (slices) бувають лише в pie chart — круговій діаграмі. Bar chart — стовпчикова.

B.q: The music and costumes really ___ the school play to life.
B.explain: Bring sth to life — оживити щось, зробити цікавішим.

example.title: My tomato talk
example.uk:
Минулої весни наш клуб садівників попросив мене розповісти, як вирощувати помідори на балконі. Я два вечори готував презентацію. Слайди я зробив простими: кілька фото, кругова діаграма моїх витрат і три головні тези великими літерами, які легко було прочитати.

У день виступу в мене тремтіли руки, тож я на мить зупинився і глибоко подихав. Потім я випрямився, подивився в очі усміхненому дідусеві в першому ряду й почав. Я попросив усіх угадати, скільки помідорів може дати один кущ, і невдовзі вся зала вигукувала числа.

Після цього я ще двадцять хвилин відповідав на запитання. Двоє навіть попросили в мене трохи насіння!
example.en:
Last spring our garden club asked me to give a talk about growing tomatoes on a balcony. I spent two evenings [[preparing my presentation|a1]]. I [[kept the slides simple|b6]]: a few photos, a [[pie chart|b11]] of what I'd spent, and three [[key points|b8]] in big letters that were [[easy to read|b7]].

On the day, my hands were shaking, so I stopped for a moment and [[breathed deeply|a12]]. Then I [[stood up straight|a8]], [[made eye contact|a10]] with a smiling old man in the front row and began. I asked everyone to guess how many tomatoes one plant can produce, and soon the whole room was shouting out numbers.

Afterwards I [[dealt with questions|a16]] for twenty minutes. Two people even asked for some of my seeds!
